lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Systems of Linear Equations and Inequalities
lessonRef.title: Concept model B: feasible regions from multiple constraints

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Compare these two examples. Find the step where they stop being the same.

items.prompt: Why may we add a multiple of one equation to another?

steps: Every common solution still satisfies the combination.
The step reverses, so nothing is gained.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt:
How many solutions does this system have?
  2x − 1y = -9
  6x − 3y = -27
choices: exactly two solutions
infinitely many solutions
no solution
exactly one solution

items.prompt: Is the point (-3, 2) in the solution region of -5x − 5y ≤ -8?
choices: Yes; substituting gives 5 ≤ -8.
The region cannot be tested without graphing it first.
No; substituting gives 5, which is greater than -8.
Only points on the boundary line are in the solution region.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 2 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.
The new system is equivalent only when 2 is 1.
The new system may lose solutions that the original had.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.

items.prompt:
How many solutions does this system have?
  5x − 3y = 11
  6x − 3y = 14
choices: exactly one solution
infinitely many solutions
exactly two solutions
no solution

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Is the point (-1, 5) in the solution region of 4x − 1y ≤ -9?
choices: Only points on the boundary line are in the solution region.
Yes; substituting gives -9 ≤ -9.
The region cannot be tested without graphing it first.
No; substituting gives -9, which is greater than -9.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 5 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.
The new system is equivalent only when 5 is 1.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.
The new system may lose solutions that the original had.
